guideTitle: The Best 400 lb Gaming Chairs, Compared by Gas Lift, Seat and Recline
metaTitle: Best Gaming Chairs with a 400 lb Weight Capacity (2026)
metaDescription: Every chair here is rated for 400 lb, so we compared what backs that figure: gas lift class, base certification, seat width, cushioning, recline and warranty.
introParagraphs: All eight chairs in this guide list a 400 lb capacity, so the rating alone doesn't separate them. What does is the evidence behind it and the fit: whether the gas lift is a Class 3 or Class 4 unit, whether the base has BIFMA testing, how wide the seat is, and how the cushion is built.

Class 4 gas lifts are generally rated for heavier loads than Class 3; several chairs here specify one, and two also list BIFMA-tested bases. Where a listing doesn't specify either, treat the 400 lb figure with a little more caution.
Our comparison is based on published specifications and certifications, not hands-on testing. Prices ranged from about $80 to $230 at the time of writing.

gtracing-big-tall-saddle-400.summary: A wingback chair with 3D saddle cushion, dual-spring lumbar and footrest, with extensive buyer feedback.
gtracing-big-tall-saddle-400.description:
The GTRACING Big & Tall is the most established chair here, with by far the largest and a very positive base of buyer feedback. That track record is its main advantage over newer listings with similar specifications.

It has a 3D saddle cushion designed to spread weight, a dual-spring lumbar, a two-sided wingback, height-adjustable armrests, a chrome metal frame, a footrest and a 90- to 150-degree recline.

The listing doesn't specify gas lift class or base certification, it costs more than several alternatives, and the frame is bulky.
gtracing-big-tall-saddle-400.bestFor: Buyers who value a long track record over certifications.
gtracing-big-tall-saddle-400.skipIf: You want a stated Class 4 lift for less; the LEMBERI has one.

lemberi-big-tall-pu-leather-400.summary: A 52.9-inch high-back chair with Class 4 gas lift, massage lumbar and footrest, under $100.
lemberi-big-tall-pu-leather-400.description:
The LEMBERI pairs a Class 4 gas lift with a price under $100 at the time of writing, and it has a large base of buyer feedback.

It has a 52.9-inch back, a thick steel frame, massage lumbar, synchronized linkage armrests, a footrest, a 90- to 155-degree recline and casters LEMBERI rates for 1,000 miles.

It is PU leather, and the listing doesn't mention a BIFMA-tested base.
lemberi-big-tall-pu-leather-400.bestFor: A tall, heavier user on a budget.
lemberi-big-tall-pu-leather-400.skipIf: You want fabric; the GTPLAYER VN-GT829 is upholstered in it.

gtplayer-vn-gt829-triple-pad-400.summary: A breathable fabric chair with a triple-pad spring seat, 52-inch back and footrest.
gtplayer-vn-gt829-triple-pad-400.description:
The GTPLAYER VN-GT829 is the fabric option: breathable fabric over a triple-pad spring seat GTPLAYER calls cloud-like, with a 52-inch back and embroidery details.

It has linkage armrests, a pull-out footrest, an SGS Class 3 gas lift, an FSC-certified wood frame and a one-year warranty.

Its gas lift is Class 3 rather than Class 4, and it has less buyer feedback than the top picks.
gtplayer-vn-gt829-triple-pad-400.bestFor: Heavier users who prefer fabric over PU leather.
gtplayer-vn-gt829-triple-pad-400.skipIf: A Class 4 lift matters to you; the LEMBERI or GTPLAYER CH6MK530 has one.

gtplayer-ch6mk530-embossing-400.summary: An embossed leather chair with Class 4 gas lift, BIFMA-tested base and wide wingless seat.
gtplayer-ch6mk530-embossing-400.description:
The GTPLAYER CH6MK530 has the strongest stated hardware here: an SGS Class 4 gas lift and a BIFMA-tested base.

It has a pocket-spring lumbar, embossed four-leaf-clover leather, a wingback with a wide wingless seat for hip room, a footrest, a 90- to 150-degree recline, FSC-certified wood and a one-year warranty.

It shares its design and certifications with the COMHOMA CH511 at a lower price at the time of writing.
gtplayer-ch6mk530-embossing-400.bestFor: Buyers who want certified hardware and a wider seat.
gtplayer-ch6mk530-embossing-400.skipIf: You want the larger track record of the identical design; the COMHOMA CH511 has more feedback.

comhoma-ch511-embossing-400.summary: The same embossed design, Class 4 lift and BIFMA-tested base as the GTPLAYER CH6MK530, with more feedback.
comhoma-ch511-embossing-400.description:
The COMHOMA CH511 matches the GTPLAYER CH6MK530's embossed leather, pocket-spring lumbar, wide wingless seat, SGS Class 4 gas lift and BIFMA-tested metal base.

Its advantage is a much larger base of buyer feedback. It has a footrest, a 90- to 150-degree recline, FSC-certified wood and a one-year warranty.

It was the most expensive chair here at the time of writing, about $70 more than the GTPLAYER version, and its feedback is somewhat less positive than most here.
pros: Larger buyer feedback than its twin
cons: Most expensive here at the time of writing
Less positive feedback than most here
comhoma-ch511-embossing-400.bestFor: Readers who want the certified embossed design with more buyer feedback.
comhoma-ch511-embossing-400.skipIf: Price matters; the GTPLAYER CH6MK530 is the same design for less.

ngen-nyx-05-pocket-spring-400.summary: A pocket-spring chair with stainless steel frame, linked armrests and footrest, under $100.
ngen-nyx-05-pocket-spring-400.description:
The N-GEN NYX-05 offers a pocket-spring cushion, stainless steel frame, synchronized linked armrests and a footrest under $100 at the time of writing.

It has an SGS Class 3 gas lift, a 90- to 135-degree recline and a one-year warranty.

Its recline is among the shallowest here, its lift is Class 3, and buyer feedback is limited so far.
ngen-nyx-05-pocket-spring-400.bestFor: A softer seat on a budget.
ngen-nyx-05-pocket-spring-400.skipIf: You want a Class 4 lift at a similar price; the LEMBERI has one.

jecqcupg-7point-support-400.summary: The lowest-priced chair here, with a 51cm extra-wide seat and 7-point support system.
jecqcupg-7point-support-400.description:
The JECQCUPG is the least expensive chair here at the time of writing, and it has an extra-wide 51cm (about 20-inch) seat of pocket springs and foam, with what JECQCUPG calls 7-point ergonomic support.

It has synchronized armrests, an SGS-rated gas lift, PU leather and a 90- to 135-degree recline. Buyer feedback is very positive, from a moderate number of reviews.

Its gas lift class isn't specified, and the recline is shallow.
jecqcupg-7point-support-400.bestFor: A wide seat for the least money.
jecqcupg-7point-support-400.skipIf: You want certified hardware; the GTPLAYER CH6MK530 lists Class 4 and BIFMA.

hesl-massage-heat-400.badge: Best for Massage, Heat and Recline
hesl-massage-heat-400.summary: A chair with 6-point vibration massage, heating, memory foam and a 160-degree recline.
hesl-massage-heat-400.description:
The HESL combines the most features here: 6-point vibration massage, heating HESL lists to 120°F, memory foam, and the deepest recline in this guide at 90 to 160 degrees.

It has self-adjusting armrests, a footrest, an SGS-rated gas lift and a 365-day parts warranty. HESL quotes about 15 minutes of assembly.

It was the second most expensive chair here at the time of writing, and massage and heat add wiring and parts.
hesl-massage-heat-400.skipIf: You don't need massage or heat; the LEMBERI reclines to 155 degrees for half the price.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Look for evidence behind the rating
buyingCriteria.explanation: A Class 4 gas lift (LEMBERI, GTPLAYER CH6MK530, COMHOMA CH511) and a BIFMA-tested base (the last two) add confidence to a 400 lb figure.
The JECQCUPG lists a 51cm seat; the GTPLAYER CH6MK530 and COMHOMA describe wide wingless seats. Several listings don't give a width.
Ranges run from 135 degrees (JECQCUPG, N-GEN) to 160 (HESL).
Most chairs here use PU leather; the GTPLAYER VN-GT829 uses fabric.

faq.q: Is a Class 4 gas lift worth it?
faq.a: For a chair used near its rated load, a Class 4 lift is generally rated for heavier loads than Class 3. The LEMBERI, GTPLAYER CH6MK530 and COMHOMA CH511 specify one.
The HESL, from 90 to 160 degrees. The JECQCUPG and N-GEN NYX-05 stop at 135.
The JECQCUPG, at about $80 at the time of writing.

faq.q: Is the LEMBERI a good alternative to the GTRACING?
faq.a: It costs less and specifies a Class 4 lift the GTRACING listing doesn't mention; the GTRACING has more buyer feedback.

faq.q: What's the difference between the GTPLAYER CH6MK530 and COMHOMA CH511?
faq.a: On paper, the same design and certifications. The COMHOMA has more buyer feedback and costs more.

bottomLine: For value, the LEMBERI is the 400 lb chair to consider first: a Class 4 lift, tall back and footrest under $100. The GTPLAYER CH6MK530 adds a BIFMA-tested base and wide seat for more, and the GTRACING offers the longest track record.
The JECQCUPG is the lowest-cost route to a wide seat, the GTPLAYER VN-GT829 the fabric option, and the HESL the pick for massage, heat and the deepest recline.
